Introduction

St. Theodota raised the unmercenary physicians Sts. Cosmas and Damian in Christian faith after their father’s death.

Background

The OCA identifies St. Theodota as the mother of the unmercenary physicians Sts. Cosmas and Damian. Its short life describes the family as natives of Asia Minor, although the familiar calendar title associates her sons with Mesopotamia. Her husband died while the children were young.

[1] Ecclesiastical biography and commemoration · Sole biographical paragraph

Family life and notable work

The account emphasizes her example and her reading of sacred books to the children. The Greek Archdiocese adds that she arranged a broad education for them, especially in medicine. Their later care of the sick without taking payment explains the title unmercenaries. The sources thus remember her through the Christian formation and education of her household.

[1] Ecclesiastical biography and commemoration · Sole biographical paragraph · [2] Ecclesiastical biography and commemoration · Reading: upbringing and medical education

What is known about her death

These short entries do not establish the circumstances or exact date of St. Theodota’s death. They do not identify this mother as a martyr. She must not be confused with other women called St. Theodota or Theodote who appear in separate martyrdom narratives.

[1] Ecclesiastical biography and commemoration · Limits of the named mother’s short entry

Commemoration

Both the OCA and Greek Archdiocese name her in the November 1 observance. The family’s received life highlights Christian parenting, education and free care for people in need.

[2] Ecclesiastical biography and commemoration · Title, date and Reading
